layers.name: Energy
layers.description: More generation and a stronger grid are foundations for industrial growth. Track dependable power for AI factories and communities, alongside storage, efficiency and affordability.
layers.connection: Delivered electricity supports chip fabrication and AI factories. New power and grid projects can also create work for local builders and equipment suppliers; realized benefits need local evidence.
focus: New generation, firm power and commissioning
Local jobs, supplier spending and electricity affordability
layers.outlook: Track new generation, grid delivery and demand together. More annual energy does not automatically provide power in the right place at the right time.

layers.name: Chips
layers.description: Compute, memory, storage and networking chips make the AI factory possible. Design, fabrication, advanced packaging and manufacturing equipment turn ideas into working silicon.
layers.connection: Accelerators need memory, storage and network connectivity. Domestic fabs and suppliers connect this layer to industrial capacity, while deployed systems connect it to useful compute.
focus: Chip designers, fabs and manufacturing equipment
Accelerators, memory, storage and advanced packaging
Networking silicon, optical connections and delivered supply
layers.outlook: Follow operational fabs and reproducible system benchmarks. Process-node names alone do not establish speed, efficiency or available AI capacity.

layers.name: Infrastructure
layers.description: AI factories bring power, chips, storage, networking and cooling together. They provide the compute for models to produce useful intelligence, generated reasoning and actions.
layers.connection: Scale up within systems, scale out across clusters, and scale across sites. Copper and optical connections help turn individual chips into capacity for training and inference.
focus: Operational capacity, grid delivery and commissioning
Local purchasing, construction work and operating jobs
layers.outlook: Follow projects from announcement through financing, construction and operation. Site counts and investment pledges are context, not delivered compute.

layers.name: Models
layers.description: Model companies and open communities build LLMs and other models. Harnesses connect them to context and tools; agent systems organize their capabilities into useful work.
layers.connection: AI factories supply compute. Models, harnesses and agent systems connect that compute to digital workers, robotics and scientific applications; reliability determines practical value.
focus: Model and agent reliability on completed tasks
Harnesses, tool use and human intervention
Inference cost, efficiency, openness and scientific capability
layers.outlook: Track capability, reliability, cost and openness separately. Better benchmark scores need to translate into dependable performance in real tasks.

layers.name: Applications
layers.description: Put intelligence to work: digital workers for companies, productive robots in the physical world, and advances in medicine, engineering, climate research and clean energy. Track demonstrated outcomes.
layers.connection: Applications turn model capability into business value and physical or scientific results. Useful demand can support the layers below; adoption alone does not establish economic benefit.
focus: Digital workers: completed work, quality and business value
Industrial, mobile and humanoid robot deployments
Healthcare, drug discovery, engineering, climate and clean energy
layers.outlook: Follow useful work from trials into sustained deployment. Measure productivity, robot reliability and validated scientific or patient outcomes; keep future ambitions distinct from demonstrated results.

events.title: August payroll data show an uneven industrial employment picture
events.summary: BLS reports a preliminary, seasonally adjusted gain of 16,000 U.S. manufacturing jobs and a decline of 23,000 information-sector jobs in August 2026. These broad sectors include activity beyond AI, so the changes cannot be attributed to AI alone.

events.title: What the August jobs report establishes
events.summary: BLS reports gains of 22,000 construction jobs and 8,000 nonresidential specialty trade jobs, a subset of construction. BLS calls overall construction little changed. These broad industry figures do not isolate electricians or AI projects.

events.title: Reading the White House article
events.summary: The administration presents the August report as evidence for its reindustrialization agenda. The ledger uses the underlying BLS release for measured payroll changes; those figures alone do not establish policy or AI causation.

events.title: Stargate is tracked campus by campus
events.summary: Epoch’s Abilene record distinguishes an estimated current IT footprint from its end-state projection. Stack Ledger now separates additional New Mexico, Wisconsin, Michigan, Ohio and Texas sites, preserving different construction and operating evidence instead of assigning the program envelope to every campus.

events.title: Indiana HBM packaging gets a revised production schedule
events.summary: SK hynix reports groundbreaking for its Indiana packaging and test facility. The updated release distinguishes cleanroom readiness from later mass production, moving beyond the older overview’s earlier operations target. Korean wafer fabrication and U.S. packaging remain separate production steps.

events.title: The electrician outlook includes AI and the grid
events.summary: BLS projects electrician employment to grow 9% over 2025–2035 and cites data centers, grid upgrades and renewable power connections among the drivers. Projected annual openings include replacement needs.

events.title: NVLink Fusion enables XPU integration with NVIDIA AI infrastructure
events.summary: NVIDIA announced NVLink Fusion to connect custom XPUs to its AI infrastructure, aiming to increase performance and accelerate time to market for semi-custom AI factories.

events.title: Cape Station advances commissioning with a phased power schedule
events.summary: Fervo reports mechanical completion on its first two GeoBlocks. Block 1 targets first power in Q4 2026, with blocks 2 and 3 following in early 2027; Phase II targets 2028. Commissioning progress should not be recorded as the entire first phase already generating.

events.title: Actual electricity output is growing alongside capacity plans
events.summary: EIA estimates U.S. electric power sector generation rose by 37 billion kWh, or 1.8%, in the first half of 2026 versus the same period in 2025. Solar and wind generation increased 21% and 6%. These are historical output changes, not nameplate additions or electricity dedicated to AI.

events.title: Terafab enters the delivery ledger as a commitment
events.summary: SpaceX identifies a Texas site and an initial investment requirement for Terafab. The ledger separates this future chip-manufacturing program from Tesla Cortex training compute and the Colossus data centers. Permits, first wafers and qualified production remain milestones to verify.

events.title: Texas grid-connection review changes the scheduling context
events.summary: ERCOT says data-center large loads must undergo verification before advancing through interconnection, and delays its planned Batch Zero classification notices. The notice does not establish that Abilene’s operating facilities have stopped or identify the effect on each expansion.

events.title: Colossus power transition has a dated removal schedule
events.summary: SpaceXAI reports a permanent Southaven power plant under construction and an agreed schedule for removing temporary turbines. Grid energization, temporary generation, the permitted future plant and the filed legal challenge are tracked separately. Actual removals and operating output require follow-up evidence.

events.title: Tesla driving and robotics retain their deployment stages
events.summary: Tesla’s shareholder update distinguishes consumer FSD supervision from city-specific Robotaxi operations. Optimus training builds and manufacturing preparations do not establish a productive deployed fleet. Cortex compute is tracked separately from driving exposure and physical work.

events.title: TSMC and Amkor extend the Arizona packaging supply chain
events.summary: The companies describe a long-term U.S. advanced-packaging partnership while Amkor’s Arizona campus and TSMC’s fabrication facilities continue development. An agreement and an expanding site do not establish commissioned packaging throughput.

events.title: Hyperion’s expanded campus remains a construction-stage plan
events.summary: Meta describes a 5 GW campus expansion and future Entergy-backed energy infrastructure. The project tracker keeps the announced rating separate from verified operational capacity and asks for generation, grid and data-center commissioning evidence.

events.title: Hyperion separates local contracts from investment plans
events.summary: Meta’s Richland Parish update distinguishes contracts awarded to Louisiana businesses from its regional investment plans and future staffing. The jobs table keeps expected peak construction work apart from promised permanent roles; contracts awarded are not labeled as cash already paid.

events.title: Grid agreements are improving, but the queue is not delivered power
events.summary: Berkeley Lab reports 2,061 GW of generation and storage active in end-2025 queues. Several regions processed record agreement volumes, while the median path to commercial operation exceeded five years in the available regional data. Queue withdrawals also contributed to the smaller backlog.

events.title: Memory capacity outlook points to further expansion
events.summary: SEMI projects global 300mm memory fabrication capacity of 4.1 million wafers per month in 2026 and 4.2 million in 2027. These are forecasts covering memory broadly, not HBM-only output or accelerator shipments.

events.title: Fairwater moves from construction plans to reported operation
events.summary: Microsoft reports its first Mount Pleasant facility fully operational, with nearly 550 full-time employees on site. Construction of the adjacent second facility continues toward a 2028 completion schedule. No commissioned-MW total is supplied in this release.

events.title: CHPE adds an operating transmission link to New York City
events.summary: The developer reports commercial operation and power deliveries on the 1,250 MW Quebec-to-New York City link. This is transmission capability, not new generating capacity. The June disclosure also identifies temporary market restrictions; later resolution remains a follow-up.

events.title: Qcells starts U.S. solar cell manufacturing
events.summary: Qcells reported starting Cartersville solar cell production in June 2026, with module assembly at full capacity. Full integrated production remained targeted for Q3, and the combined Georgia workforce figure was an expectation, not verified hiring.

events.title: Model capability needs a reliability threshold
events.summary: METR’s current Time Horizon 1.1 page distinguishes 50% and 80% success on software tasks measured in human-expert time. It warns that measurements above 16 hours are unreliable with its current task suite. These results do not establish dependable autonomy across ordinary jobs.

events.title: Waymo operating service has a measurable footprint
events.summary: Alphabet reports fully autonomous rides across an expanded U.S. service footprint. The ledger keeps this disclosure separate from Waymo’s older explicitly paid-trip run-rate, commercial vehicle count and rider-only safety mileage, retaining each record’s geography and date.

events.title: A clearer view of the power ahead
events.summary: The IEA’s updated outlook puts global data-center electricity consumption at roughly 950 TWh in 2030, from 485 TWh in 2025. Grid delivery and equipment supply remain important to realizing that growth.

events.title: New inference results broaden the measurement toolkit
events.summary: MLPerf Inference v6.0 adds a GPT-OSS 120B workload and an interactive DeepSeek-R1 scenario permitting speculative decoding. Compare compatible workloads, quality targets, accelerator counts and serving scenarios. Throughput results do not by themselves measure dollar cost or application reliability.

events.title: Inference price-performance research extends the cost picture
events.summary: A revised research paper estimates roughly 5–10-fold annual declines in the price of achieving a fixed benchmark performance level across several task families. This is a retrospective benchmark-based estimate, not a guarantee that frontier API prices or every real task get cheaper at that rate.

events.title: Coherent optical engines · demonstration announced
events.summary: Coherent announced OFC demonstrations of several CPO architectures and components. This is a demonstration announcement, not evidence of installed production capacity.

events.title: A longer horizon for firm power
events.summary: DOE describes a 400 GW U.S. nuclear capacity goal for 2050. It is an economy-wide ambition; tracking operational additions will help distinguish the target from delivered power.

events.title: Lightmatter Passage · sampling reported
events.summary: Lightmatter reported Passage chiplet sampling and a throughput demonstration. Sampling is earlier than volume deployment.

events.title: Samsung reports commercial HBM4 shipments
events.summary: Samsung says HBM4 mass production has begun and commercial products have shipped. This establishes a product milestone, not a verified industry-wide output rate; comparable shipment volumes and packaging throughput remain research gaps.

events.title: AWS reports deployed accelerator supply and production workloads
events.summary: Amazon reports 1.4 million Trainium2 chips landed across its fleet and more than 500,000 in the operational Rainier cluster. Rainier is a subset of the fleet, so these counts must not be added. The same release says Trainium3 is delivering production workloads.

events.title: Marvell / Celestial AI · acquisition completed
events.summary: Marvell completed the acquisition of Celestial AI. Its optical scale-up technology now belongs within the Marvell profile; acquisition value is not product revenue.

events.title: Fiber supply also creates industrial work
events.summary: Corning’s Meta agreement is for up to $6 billion over multiple years and supports a North Carolina expansion. Its employment language includes sustaining an existing workforce, not 5,000 newly created jobs.

events.title: Micron announces New York groundbreaking; production expected in 2030
events.summary: Micron announced the groundbreaking for its New York memory complex, with up to four fabs planned. The company expects production to start in 2030 and ramp through the decade. Its regional jobs projection is a long-term impact claim, not a count of workers already hired.

events.title: Solar manufacturing delivers reported Louisiana employment
events.summary: First Solar’s inauguration release reports a $1.1 billion Louisiana facility and more than 700 current employees. Manufacturing began in July 2025; the later staffing target and full-ramp module capacity remain distinct from that reported milestone.

events.title: Another chapter in Wisconsin’s buildout
events.summary: Microsoft announced an additional $4 billion commitment for a second Wisconsin data center over three years. The pledge is tracked separately from completed construction and actual expenditure.

events.title: AlphaGenome supplies measured scientific prediction results
events.summary: DeepMind reports gains on DNA-sequence and regulatory-variant prediction evaluations; its research page notes Nature publication in January 2026. These are research prediction outcomes, not evidence of new treatments or demonstrated clinical benefit.

events.title: Broadcom Bailly CPO · volume production reported
events.summary: Broadcom described its Tomahawk 5-Bailly CPO generation as in volume production while announcing a newer generation. That does not establish universal CPO adoption.

events.title: Training capacity matters
events.summary: IBEW’s May 2025 reporting describes rising data-center labor demand and a nearly tripled apprenticeship program at Baltimore Local 24. This is a dated local union account, not a national hiring statistic.

events.title: Transformer investment links grid demand to manufacturing jobs
events.summary: Eaton announced a $340 million Jonesville transformer manufacturing investment, with production and hiring for 700 local jobs expected to begin in 2027. The 2025 disclosure remains a plan until delivery evidence is reviewed.

events.title: Power equipment expansion includes a U.S. workforce commitment
events.summary: GE Vernova announced almost $600 million for U.S. factories and facilities over two years, with approximately 1,500 expected factory and engineering jobs. This is a dated investment and hiring plan; realized employment remains a follow-up question.

events.title: Customer-support field evidence goes beyond adoption counts
events.summary: The revised Generative AI at Work paper studies 5,172 support agents and reports a 15% average increase in issues resolved per hour, with heterogeneous effects. This is historical evidence from a particular workplace setting, not a 2026 economy-wide productivity estimate.

events.title: An advanced manufacturing milestone
events.summary: TSMC reports that its 2 nm technology entered high-volume manufacturing in the fourth quarter of 2025. Its annual report also describes expanding manufacturing capacity across regions.

events.title: Useful model capability became more affordable
events.summary: Stanford’s 2025 AI Index records a drop from $20 to $0.07 per million tokens at a GPT-3.5-equivalent benchmark threshold between November 2022 and October 2024.

events.title: AI reaches more organizations
events.summary: The 2026 AI Index reports organizational AI adoption of 88%, following 78% in the previous report. These survey results track use; measured business outcomes remain a separate research question.

events.title: Veo 3 zero-shot video reasoning
events.summary: Google DeepMind’s Veo 3 demonstrated zero-shot abilities to simulate physical behaviors like buoyancy and maze solving across more than 18,000 generated videos, indicating emergent video reasoning without task-specific training.

targets.title: Plan for global data-center electricity demand
targets.detail: Demand projection for all data centers. A matched generation-and-grid delivery series is needed to assess readiness.

targets.title: Expand U.S. nuclear generating capacity
targets.detail: Economy-wide target. The approximate starting fleet is not a current measurement of additions toward the goal.

targets.title: Build a second Wisconsin data center
targets.detail: Three-year spending pledge. We need subsequent expenditure and commissioning evidence before assessing delivery.
